name: Kasairinkaikoen
tagline: Tokyo in 18 minutes and Otemachi in 24 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥60,000 to ¥70,000.
summary: The station is in Edogawa City, served by JR Keiyo Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 24 minutes to Otemachi, 38 minutes to Shinjuku, 45 minutes to Shibuya and 32 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥60,000 to ¥70,000. The station stands 4.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 7.6 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 4.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 2.8 m to 10.4 m, a difference of 7.6 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, neither the station nor any of the nine points within 400 m of it falls inside the projected inundation area. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station, OpenStreetMap records neither a clinic nor a pharmacy. The nearest hospital is 東京臨海病院, about 19 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 東京脳神経センター病院, about 32 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: JR Keiyo Line.
congestion: JR Keiyo Line runs at 123% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 葛西臨海公園→新木場, which includes this station. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥60,000 to ¥70,000 and 1K ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. 1LDK ¥130,000 to ¥140,000 and 2LDK ¥170,000 to ¥180,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

neighbours.lead: Nishi-Kasai is ahead on the number of medical facilities and how easy the shopping is, but Kasairinkaikoen is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: About 2.5 km from Kasairinkaikoen in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi 3 minutes sooner than Kasairinkaikoen. One-room rents run about ¥8,000 higher.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: OpenStreetMap records no supermarket within walking distance of the station.
leads.hazards: Neither the station nor the ground around it falls inside the projected flood area.
leads.stationNote: Only the JR Keiyo Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the lowest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the low side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are very lightly loaded in the morning.
